description: Six independent polyphonic utility sections in one panel: a buffered multiple, an inverter with two rectifiers, a precision adder, a minimum and maximum pair, a mixer, and a sample and hold

params.text: Applies a third of the gain to the 3:1 mix, matching the hardware, so that its output is the average of the three inputs rather than their sum

inputs.text: The signal the three 1:3 outputs copy; the channel count of this cable sets the polyphony of that section
One of the two signals the 2:2 section adds; the larger channel count of the two sets the polyphony of that section
One of the three signals the 3:1 section mixes; the largest channel count of the three sets the polyphony of that section
The signal the three SIGN outputs shape; the channel count of this cable sets the polyphony of that section
The first signal the LOGIC section compares; the larger channel count of the two inputs sets the polyphony of that section
The second signal the LOGIC section compares; the larger channel count of the two inputs sets the polyphony of that section
The signal the sample and hold reads; with nothing patched it reads the module's own noise generator instead, which turns the section into a random voltage source
A rising edge past 1V takes a reading on each channel; the channel count of this cable sets the polyphony of the sample and hold section

outputs.text: A copy of the 1:3 input at the same voltage
The two 2:2 inputs added together; with one of them patched alone this is a copy of it, which makes the section a one-into-two multiple
The three 3:1 inputs added together, or their average when the HW button is on
The SIGN input with its sign flipped, so that 5V in gives -5V out
The SIGN input with everything below 0V held at 0V, which adds harmonics to an audio signal
The SIGN input with everything below 0V flipped above it, which doubles the apparent frequency of a symmetrical wave
Whichever of the two LOGIC inputs is lower at each instant, which acts as an analogue AND; with one input patched alone it carries that signal's negative half
Whichever of the two LOGIC inputs is higher at each instant, which acts as an analogue OR; with one input patched alone it carries that signal's positive half
The noise generator, one independent channel for each channel the sample and hold trigger carries
The voltage read on each channel at the last trigger, held until the next trigger arrives on that channel

notes: the six sections are independent: each takes its polyphony from its own inputs, and none of them feeds another.
the lamp in each section reports the voltage that section is working on, with one pair of colours for a monophonic cable and another for a polyphonic one.
held voltages are not saved: they are lost when Rack closes.
menu: Noise mode: White noise (High CPU), Prism noise (Low CPU) — picks which noise generator feeds the NOISE output and the unpatched sample and hold input

polyphonic

unpatched it reads the module's noise generator.
